text:
marta: quick note  new users ran the tutorial and got 401s after customer rotated keys. looks like confusion around env var name + org vs project-scoped keys.

owen: are they using REDWOOD_API_KEY like our README or something else?

marta: some copied an internal snippet that uses REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY; others used REDWOOD_TOKEN. ugh.

lee: that's a new bad pattern. we never documented REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY publicly. accidental leak from an old repo. SDKs don't accept it, so they fail.

owen: we should do two things: 1) make SDKs accept a canonical whitelist (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN) and warn on unknown names; 2) add a devex check on the server that surfaces when a presented key looks project-scoped vs org-scoped. return a clearer 401 message.

marta: support is spending time repro-ing. can we add a short troubleshooting blurb in the sampleapp: "If you see 401 after rotation, check env var name and whether your key is project-scoped. Use an org-scoped key for the tutorial."

support: yes please. also request: a CLI helper that prints platform-specific export lines so users can paste quickly after rotation. small thing but reduces support loops.

lee: agree. proposal for CLI: `rw auth export --format bash|ps1|cmd` -> prints the right commands and a note about scope.

owen: on the SDK side, let's stop retrying on 401 and surface an enriched message: "401 Unauthorized: possible causes include rotated key, project-scoped key, or wrong env var name. Run `rw auth export --format bash` to rehydrate."

marta: we'll also scan docs/repos for REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY and archival-delete those snippets. one-off cleanup.

support: filing backlog item for the docs sweep and adding the troubleshooting blurb to the onboarding checklist. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
